concepts.definition: Sea-surface height relative to the moving land at a location; combines ocean change, vertical land motion, and regional effects.
Land elevation below a specified water surface in a static elevation model, sometimes conditioned on hydraulic connection.
not_equivalent_to: permanent inundation when defenses are present

concepts.definition: Flooding when water levels exceed locally defined minor, moderate, or major thresholds; days are threshold-exceedance projections, not days when a whole city floods.
Persistent occupation of unprotected low land by mean or tidal water after accounting for hydraulic connectivity and adaptation.
Abnormal coastal water-level rise produced by a storm, superimposed on tides and mean sea level.
The practical ability to live and operate safely with reliable housing, access, drainage, drinking water, wastewater, electricity, insurance, finance, health care, and emergency services.

cities.geographic_guardrail: Keep City of New Orleans, metropolitan New Orleans, the Ohenhen study domain, the NOAA 30 N / 90 W grid, New Canal Station, and Grand Isle separate.
physical_setting: Much of the city is below sea level and surrounded by levees.
Rainfall must be removed through an engineered drainage system.
Coastal-wetland loss and subsidence alter the regional hazard context.

risk_pathways.mechanism: Ocean rise plus high local vertical-land-motion contribution increases water levels relative to land.
Natural compaction and human-influenced groundwater or sediment processes vary spatially.
Tropical-cyclone surge acts on the changing coastal baseline and protection system.
Intense rainfall can exceed inlet, pipe, canal, pump, or power capacity even when surge defenses hold.

engineered_dependencies.guardrail: Not zero risk and not one flood per century.

engineered_dependencies.capacity_or_standard: 24 drainage pump stations; 50,891 cubic feet per second listed by the city
engineered_dependencies.guardrail: Nominal capacity is not equivalent to delivered capacity in every storm or neighborhood.

time_anchors.value: National Nature study horizon; do not convert to city disappearance.

time_anchors.guardrail: 30 N / 90 W one-degree grid, not a parcel-depth map.
Louisiana coastwide scenario range, not land inside New Orleans.

habitability_sequence: service interruptions and access failures become more frequent
households with fewer resources face earlier displacement
protection or accommodation upgrades are required
managed relocation may become necessary in selected areas
cities.headline: New Orleans' danger is protection dependence under rising relative water levels—not a defensible single date when the whole city disappears.

cities.geographic_guardrail: Keep City of Miami, Miami-Dade County, the Ohenhen Miami study domain, and the Virginia Key tide gauge separate. The Nature study's exposed area can exceed the City of Miami's land area because its domain is broader.
physical_setting: Low coastal elevations create tidal and surge exposure.
Highly permeable limestone allows groundwater and seawater to bypass surface barriers.
Canals connect coastal level, groundwater, and drainage performance.
The Biscayne aquifer is the primary drinking-water source.

risk_pathways.mechanism: Higher coastal water increases tidal flooding and reduces gravity-drainage performance.
Permeable limestone transmits coastal water inland and raises the water table.
Sea-level pressure, withdrawals, canals, and freshwater levels affect the inland salt front.
Storm water enters from the ocean and back bay; risk is modified but not removed by structural, nonstructural, and nature-based measures.

system_dependencies.capacity_or_standard: Miami-Dade reports 99% of groundwater withdrawn comes from the aquifer.
system_dependencies.guardrail: Groundwater withdrawal share is not the same as total delivered water without checking system accounting.

system_dependencies.capacity_or_standard: County program cites approximately 120,000 residential and commercial properties on septic systems.
system_dependencies.guardrail: Property count is countywide and program-era; do not label all systems failed.

time_anchors.guardrail: SSP2-4.5; study-domain exposure; defenses and estimates vary; not municipal inundation.
Planning range referenced to Key West, not uniform water depth.
Station scenario span; scenario values are not probabilities.

habitability_sequence: more frequent tide and rainfall interaction
groundwater and outfall constraints emerge in low areas
septic, roads, utilities, and buildings require adaptation
insurance and housing affordability pressures change who can remain
large-scale public works and building-level adaptation expand
selective retreat may be required where protection and accommodation are infeasible
cities.headline: Miami's earliest functional risks can come through groundwater, drainage, water quality, and affordability—not only an advancing ocean shoreline.

new_orleans_distinctive: very high coastal-Louisiana relative trend and wetland context
miami_distinctive: surface walls cannot alone isolate the urban hydrologic system
